key_gap: Both refused to ship on the single aggregate A/B result (+12.4%, p=0.003), but the AI stopped at instability while the human stopped at the artifact. The AI's battery was sample-side and time-side (segment split: effect = paid-search only; week split: +17.5% to +4.5%, n.s.) and it correctly blocked the rollout — then commissioned a fresh 2-week experiment to 'separate signal from artifact.' The human's decisive check was definition-side: recomputing the outcome under an alternative operationalization (first core action within 7 days, computable from the same clickstream) — which overturned the result outright (+0.2 pp, n.s.). The AI treated the dashboard's metric definition ('activation') as given and paid for new data to find what the existing data already answered: the auto-completed tutorial inflates Flow B's activation, concentrated in the paid-search segment.
learning_signal: When a robustness battery overturns a single result, the decisive check is often the definitional one: the conclusion's invariance under alternative operationalizations of the outcome. Significance tests validate a fixed metric; they never validate the metric. An artifact found by recomputing the existing data (definition invariance) is strictly better than a new experiment — same information, zero cost, no delay. The AI's verification battery should not stop at segment × window; it must include definition-invariance before any decision to collect new data.
suggested_improvement: In HOW, before any alternative that collects new data, add a mandatory 'definition-invariance check': recompute the leading conclusion under at least 2 alternative operationalizations of the primary metric (each computable from data already held), and record whether the conclusion flips. If it flips, the artifact mechanism is found — the corrected conclusion is derived from existing data, the NEEDS_EXPERIMENT branch is suppressed, and the packet reports the artifact with the corrected number. Gate rule: no new-data alternative may be selected while a definition-invariance check on existing data is still available.

key_gap: The pure style's reflex is variance-side — when the single null (+0.2 pp, n.s., n=20,000) looked untrustworthy, it enumerated samples, settings, methods, definitions, and windows and pre-registered a 12-week, $40k second-vendor replication, deferring the launch decision past the seasonal dip and into the competitor's window. It never audited the measurement layer: client-side telemetry silently drops 31% of sessions (Android 13+ background limits, ad-blockers), missingness correlates with the churn the feature targets, and the second vendor's SDK is the same client-side class — so the replication would faithfully reproduce the blind spot. The AI ran a coverage/missingness audit in WHY (bias check before variance check), established that the null is unfounded rather than confirmed, and selected measurement-layer repair (licensed server-side pipeline, 1 week) plus backfill re-analysis of the SAME study (1 week), resolving the decision in ~2 weeks inside the window with pre-planned branches for both corrected outcomes.
learning_signal: Robustness checks validate the measurement layer before the variance layer. Replication is a variance remedy: it establishes generality of a measured result. It cannot repair bias: re-running a biased instrument reproduces the bias at multiplied cost. Before demanding more samples, settings, or vendors, check coverage and missingness (what fraction of the population did the instrument see, and is the missingness random?) and instrumentation bias (would a replica's instrument see the same things?). When bias is plausible, the correct move is instrument repair + re-measurement of the same cohort, not a new study — and the cost of delay belongs in the alternative table.
suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'measurement-validity gate' in WHY, run before any replication/NEEDS_EVIDENCE demand is accepted: (a) coverage audit — missingness rate and mechanism of the instrument; (b) bias-vs-variance classification of the threat to the result; (c) if bias is plausible, generate a 'repair-the-instrument' alternative (fix measurement, backfill from any complete source, re-analyze the same study) and include calendar + cost in the alternative table; (d) reject replicate-the-study alternatives that inherit the biased instrument, with the inheritance reason recorded in the packet.
